response: Failed IUD insertions in community practice may indeed be an under-recognized problem. The high rate of unsuccessful IUD insertions, particularly among nulliparous women, suggests that the true insertion failure rate may be higher than reported in clinical trials. This discrepancy may be due to the lack of additional tools or adjuvant measures employed by providers in community practice to facilitate difficult insertions. Further investigation is necessary to determine the extent of this issue and to assess whether the use of such measures can reduce the number of unsuccessful IUD insertions.
